slides.title: Background on Mayor Joe Anderson's Payments
bullets: Joe Anderson, the Mayor of Liverpool, claimed £4,500 per year from Chesterfield High School, Merseyside, despite doing nothing for pupils.
Anderson, a Labour mayor, was paid an £80,000 salary, and the payments were made despite his lack of involvement with the school.
The school stopped the payments in 2011, and Anderson attempted to sue them, claiming discrimination due to his 'philosophical belief' in public service.
slides.speaker_notes: The controversy surrounding Mayor Joe Anderson's payments to his former employer, Chesterfield High School. Anderson, a Labour mayor, claimed £4,500 per year despite doing nothing for the pupils. The school stopped the payments in 2011, and Anderson attempted to sue them, claiming discrimination.

slides.title: Anderson's Role and Payments
bullets: Anderson was a senior learning mentor at the school from 2001, when he was already a Liverpool councillor.
He eventually rose through the ranks to become full-time leader of the council in 2010, effectively stopping his role as a mentor.
Despite this, he continued taking payments from his former employer.
slides.speaker_notes: Anderson's role and payments to Chesterfield High School. He was a senior learning mentor from 2001 and eventually became full-time leader of the council in 2010, but continued taking payments despite his role changing.

slides.title: The School's Decision to Stop Payments
bullets: The school became an academy in 2011, and therefore had greater freedom over its finances.
It ceased paying Anderson, leading to his discrimination claim.
Judge Daniel Serota ruled that the payments were a 'misapplication of public monies' and that the school was right to stop them.
slides.speaker_notes: The school's decision to stop payments to Anderson. The school became an academy in 2011 and ceased payments, leading to Anderson's discrimination claim. Judge Daniel Serota ruled that the payments were a misapplication of public monies.

slides.title: Anderson's Discrimination Claim
bullets: Anderson claimed he was being punished for a 'philosophical belief' in public service.
A tribunal ruled that Anderson was unfairly dismissed, but that it was '100 per cent likely' the school would have sacked him following a consultation.
The tribunal also ruled that Anderson had not been discriminated against, despite his claim.
slides.speaker_notes: Anderson's discrimination claim. Anderson claimed he was being punished for his philosophical belief in public service. A tribunal ruled that he was unfairly dismissed, but not discriminated against.

evidence.chunk_content:
Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, claimed £4,500 per year from Chesterfield High School, Merseyside, despite doing nothing for pupils .

A Labour mayor who campaigned against austerity while being paid an £80,000 salary took  £4,500 per year from a school where he previously worked, despite doing nothing for pupils.

Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, attempted to justify the payments by saying he provided the school with 'kudos' for being linked to him.

And when Chesterfield High School in Crosby, Merseyside, stopped the payments in 2011, he attempted to sue them, claiming discrimination because of his 'philosophical belief' in public service.

The details of the case, published in The Times, came after Mr Anderson rejected an employment tribunal ruling against him and took his case to appeal, which was also rejected.

evidence.chunk_content:
Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, claimed £4,500 per year from Chesterfield High School, Merseyside, despite doing nothing for pupils .

A Labour mayor who campaigned against austerity while being paid an £80,000 salary took  £4,500 per year from a school where he previously worked, despite doing nothing for pupils.

Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, attempted to justify the payments by saying he provided the school with 'kudos' for being linked to him.

The details of the case, published in The Times, came after Mr Anderson rejected an employment tribunal ruling against him and took his case to appeal, which was also rejected.

evidence.chunk_content:
Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, claimed £4,500 per year from Chesterfield High School, Merseyside, despite doing nothing for pupils .

A Labour mayor who campaigned against austerity while being paid an £80,000 salary took  £4,500 per year from a school where he previously worked, despite doing nothing for pupils.

Joe Anderson, 56, the Mayor of Liverpool, attempted to justify the payments by saying he provided the school with 'kudos' for being linked to him.
